_doc: PLACEHOLDER — the radial CLUSTER SHELL: west alcove anchor, aperture scrims, ceiling-witness geometry, per-era cluster states, the per-era LIGHT RIGS (the cold-light-winning arc, REINTERP_3D_STYLE_DIRECTION §1-2), and the point-cloud Close parameters. Read behind ?reinterp=1 only. COLOR LAW: every hex here already exists in data/room/era1.json — rebalanced/reused, never invented; when era2+ theme palettes land in src/desktop/theme/, the e2-e4 rig hues re-derive from them (flagged, do not treat these as final art). Occupant ids are non-display slugs (which identity's alcove this is per era — E4's exact split is a cluster-morph content call, see _note). Cluster states: sealed (E1 pre-reveal: architecture felt as shadow) → dim (O7 first-filing: dimly legible) → open (E2+: the radial grammar as the new normal).

westAlcove._note: Mirror of the fluid niche's -110° arc, west wall, in the clear gap left of the bed's head wall run. Holds the OTHER non-lead identity per era (3-cluster lean). E4: the trans niche flips forward as Maya's room (geometry doc §3.2); which of gayman/lesbian this alcove carries in E4 vs a paired presence is a cluster-morph content question — id below is a working default, not canon.

ceilingWitness._note: R8-3: presence only — light/eye-motif, NEVER reading. A square iris (pixel discipline: 90° geometry) recessed in the ceiling over the room's center; a pale sourceless wash when awake. Dormant until the O7 first filing.

rigs._note: Per-era light targets for the era1.json light ids + scene ambient. The arc: E1 lamp-dominant night (~70/30 warm, Session 7 values restated) → E2 office-grade fluorescent (~50/50, managed, shadows short) → E3 platform pastel (near-shadowless diffuse, the lamp a leftover) → E4 interface-lit near-dark (the cold has won; the lamp survives as the one warm pocket). 'close' kills the room for the point-cloud inversion.

pointCloud._note: The Close's constellation (R1 confirmed; Gephi-style reference, Round 2): warm orange/yellow NODES on a cool blue LINK-WEB, dense center + scattered satellites, labels sub-legible (here: none at all). The inversion: the warm-node/cool-web split differentiates it from the Watcher's cold data grammar — the lamp's temperature at network scale. Hues = the lamp pool (#F7C775/#EFA13F), the moon face (#F3EAD8), the moonlight blue (#6C7BA8).
